title: WPSS/2207/2014 of Yashpal Singh Bisht Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 2207 of 2014
Yashpal Singh Bisht Ö Petitioner
Vs
State of Uttarakhand & others Ö Respondents
With
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 2208 of 2014
Saroj Arya Ö Petitioner
Vs
State of Uttarakhand & others Ö Respondents
Mr. Prashant Khanna, Advocate, present for the petitioners.
Mr. N.P. Sah, Standing Counsel, present for the State.
Mr. Pankaj Chaturvedi, Advocate holding brief of Mr. Rakesh Thapliyal, Advocate, preset for
respondent No. 3.
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
1. The petitioners, in both the writ petitions, were
the candidates for the post of State Supervisor in Co-operative Department. The selection was conducted by a
Government body known as Uttarakhand Board of
Technical Education (from hereinafter referred to as
ìTechnical Boardî), which is impleaded in the present writ
petition as respondent No. 3.
2. The total number of posts, on which the
selections were to be made, are 146. The petitioners
appeared in the written examination in which Yashpal
Singh Bisht scored 77.25 marks and Saroj Arya scored
69.75 marks respectively. They were selected, however,
they were not amongst the first top 146 candidates, who
were called for verification of the documents, however, out
of these 146 candidates only 117 candidates were came
forward for verification of documents and were
recommended by the Technical Board to the State
Government. In continuation of the same selection
process, thereafter 29 candidates were asked for the
remaining posts to come forward with the credentials and

2
verification of their documents, out of which only five
candidates were found satisfied and the Technical Board
recommended their names on 19.10.2013. The names of
both the petitioners are figured in the said
recommendation. However, the appointment has not been
given to them. Hence, they preferred present writ petitions
before this Court.
3. As far as Technical Board is concerned it has
filed its counter affidavit today in the Court stating therein
that the petitioners were called for document verification
for the remaining 29 vacant posts, and after verification of
the documents, their names were recommended to the
State Government for appointment. Therefore, as far as
the contention of the selection body is concerned, it is
supporting the case of the petitioners. However, the
objection of the State Government is that there was no
provision of waiting list in the said examination, as it was
the examination not for one Department but for various
departments.
4. The petitioners, on the other hand, contend that
they are not the one who figured in the select list but their
contention is that selection itself was not complete. The
question of waiting list would commence only after the
selected candidates have dully joined the vacant posts.
The petitioners have relied upon a decision of Honíble Apex
Court in State of Jammu & Kashmir & others Vs Sat
Pal reported in 2013 (11) SCC 737 where it has been
stated that a waiting list would start to operate only when
offers of appointment have been issued to the selected
candidates. The existence of a waiting list, allows room to

3
the appointing authority to fill up vacancies which arise
during the subsistence of the waiting list. A waiting list
begins to operate, after the vacancies for which the
recruitment process has been conducted have been filled
up.
5. In the present case, however, it cannot be said
that the waiting list has commenced, as appointment
letters have not been issued to all the selected candidates
as of now. However, the selection process has not come to
an end. The petitioners were the candidates in the same
examination, they have qualified the examination and
subject to disqualification of such candidates, who have
scored higher marks than the petitioners, they must be
called for document verification and once their documents
found to be in order, their names be recommended by the
Technical Board.
6. The objections of the State Government is
therefore not correct.
7. In view thereof, the writ petitions are allowed. A
mandamus is hereby issued to the respondents/authority
concerned to consider the candidature of the petitioners on
the post of State Supervisor, unless there is any
disqualification attached to them.
8. Let the needful be done within a period of two
weeks from the date of production of a certified copy of this
order.
(Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
10.04.2015
Aswal
